title: Mock 5 · Full Syllabus Sweep
blurb: Working-capital cycle, dilution, terminal value, hedge ratio, Jensen's alpha, quiet periods and candlestick basics.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes futures from forwards?
options: Forwards are traded on exchanges; futures are private OTC contracts
Futures are standardised exchange-traded contracts with clearing-corporation guarantee; forwards are customised OTC contracts
Futures give a right but not an obligation
Forwards are marked to market daily
questions.explanation: Futures are standardised, exchange-traded, marked to market daily and guaranteed by the clearing corporation. Forwards are bilateral, customised and carry counterparty risk.
hints: Daily mark-to-market is a feature of futures, not forwards.

questions.q: Shares with differential voting rights (DVR) typically:
options: Carry fewer voting rights than ordinary shares and often trade at a discount to them
Carry no economic rights at all
Are debt instruments with a fixed coupon
Must be converted into bonds after three years
questions.explanation: DVR shares are equity shares with voting rights different (usually lower) from ordinary shares; they often trade at a discount, sometimes with a higher dividend to compensate.
hints: DVR holders do get economic rights such as dividends.
There is no such conversion feature.

questions.q: A sharp, sustained rise in crude oil prices is most likely to hurt the earnings of:
questions.explanation: Crude derivatives are key raw materials for paints, so higher crude raises input costs and squeezes margins. Upstream producers and their service providers tend to benefit.
hints: Upstream producers gain from higher realisations.
Higher oil prices usually raise activity for service providers.
Correct - crude is a major input cost.

questions.q: As per the commonly used classification in India, an investment by a foreign investor is treated as FDI rather than FPI when the stake in a listed company is:
questions.explanation: A foreign investment of 10% or more of the post-issue paid-up equity of a listed company is treated as FDI; below 10% is portfolio investment (FPI).
hints: FDI does not require majority control.

questions.q: Higher sales of two-wheelers and consumer durables every year around Diwali is an example of a:
questions.explanation: Seasonal trends are recurring calendar-linked patterns (festivals, monsoon). Secular trends are long-term structural; cyclical trends follow the business cycle.
hints: Secular trends are long-term, multi-year shifts.
Cyclical trends follow economic expansions and contractions.
A structural break is a one-time shift, not a yearly pattern.

questions.q: The threat of new entrants into an industry is LOW when:
options: Entry requires very large capital investment and government licences
Products are undifferentiated and easy to make
Distribution channels are open to all
questions.explanation: High entry barriers - large capital needs, licences, scale economies, brand loyalty and switching costs - keep the threat of new entrants low.
hints: No switching costs makes it easy for entrants to win customers.

questions.q: The shift of profits from standalone music-CD sellers to music-streaming platforms is an example of:
questions.explanation: Value migration describes profits moving from outdated business designs to new ones that better meet customer needs, often driven by technology.
hints: Seasonality is a recurring calendar pattern.
Backwardation is a commodity futures term.

questions.q: Over four quarters, the share of promoter holding that is pledged has risen from 10% to 65%. This is best viewed as:
options: A red flag, as a price fall could trigger margin calls and forced selling
questions.explanation: High and rising pledges suggest promoter financial stress; a fall in price may force lenders to sell pledged shares, adding pressure and possibly a change in control.
hints: Pledging indicates borrowing need, not confidence.
A sharp increase is not neutral.

questions.q: A company carries inventory of ₹90 crore and its annual cost of goods sold is ₹730 crore. Its inventory days (365-day year) are:
questions.explanation: Inventory days = inventory / COGS x 365 = 90 / 730 x 365 = 45 days.
hints: 8.1 is the inventory turnover (times), not days.

questions.q: A company has inventory days of 45, receivable days of 60 and payable days of 30. Its cash conversion cycle is:
questions.explanation: CCC = inventory days + receivable days - payable days = 45 + 60 - 30 = 75 days.
hints: This adds payable days instead of subtracting.

questions.q: A company's PAT rises from ₹100 crore to ₹120 crore, but its share count rises from 10 crore to 12.5 crore after a QIP. The new EPS is:
questions.explanation: New EPS = 120 / 12.5 = ₹9.60, down from ₹10.00. Profit grew 20% but equity dilution of 25% reduced per-share earnings.
hints: This divides old PAT by new shares.

questions.q: In a demerger, shareholders of the parent company typically:
options: Must pay cash to buy shares of the new company
Lose their shares in the parent
Receive bonds of the demerged company
Receive shares of the resulting (demerged) company in a set ratio, in addition to their parent shares
questions.explanation: In a demerger the separated business is housed in a new company and its shares are allotted to the parent's shareholders in a specified ratio; they continue to hold parent shares.
hints: No payment is required from shareholders.
They receive equity shares, not bonds.

questions.q: A stock trades at a P/E of 25x. Its earnings yield is:
questions.explanation: Earnings yield = EPS / price = 1 / (P/E) = 1/25 = 4%.
hints: That is the P/E itself, not a yield.

questions.q: Free cash flow in the final forecast year is ₹100 crore. It is expected to grow at 5% forever and the discount rate is 12%. The terminal value at the end of the forecast period (Gordon growth) is:
hints: This forgets to grow the final-year FCF by 5%.
This divides by g instead of (r - g).

questions.q: Sum-of-the-parts (SOTP) valuation is most appropriate for:
options: A conglomerate with distinct businesses such as cement, telecom and retail
A single-product start-up with no revenue
A company whose only asset is cash
questions.explanation: SOTP values each segment with the most suitable method and adds them up - ideal for diversified groups whose businesses have very different growth and risk profiles.
hints: A single business needs no segment split.
Bonds are valued by discounting cash flows.
A cash shell is valued at its cash.

questions.q: The correlation between spot and futures price changes is 0.8; the standard deviation of spot price changes is 3% and of futures price changes is 4%. The minimum-variance hedge ratio is:
questions.explanation: Hedge ratio = ρ x σS / σF = 0.8 x 3/4 = 0.60.
hints: Correlation alone is not the hedge ratio.
This inverts the volatility ratio (0.8 x 4/3).

questions.q: A fund returned 18% with a beta of 1.2. The risk-free rate was 6% and the market returned 14%. The fund's Jensen's alpha is:
questions.explanation: CAPM expected return = 6 + 1.2 x (14 - 6) = 15.6%. Alpha = 18 - 15.6 = 2.4%.
hints: This is Rp - Rm, ignoring beta.

questions.q: An analyst estimates intrinsic value of ₹400 per share; the stock trades at ₹300. The margin of safety is:
questions.explanation: Margin of safety = (IV - price) / IV = (400 - 300) / 400 = 25%.
hints: This divides by price instead of intrinsic value (that is the upside).

questions.q: In a well-structured equity research report, the investment thesis and recommendation should ideally appear:
options: Upfront, on the first page or summary
questions.explanation: Busy readers need the conclusion first: a good report puts the rating, target price and key thesis upfront, followed by supporting analysis.
hints: Tables support, not replace, the thesis.

questions.q: A research entity that acted as manager or co-manager of an IPO must not publish research on the issuer for how many days after the IPO is priced?
questions.explanation: The quiet period is 40 days after pricing for an IPO and 10 days for a further public offer (for managers/co-managers).
hints: 10 days applies to further public offers.
25 days applies to IPO underwriters' reports from the offering date.

questions.q: Under the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, an insider who possesses unpublished price-sensitive information (UPSI):
options: May trade if the quantity is small
Must not trade in the company's securities while in possession of UPSI (subject to specified defences)
May trade after informing the broker
May freely share it with clients for research
questions.explanation: Trading while in possession of UPSI is prohibited, and UPSI may be communicated only for legitimate purposes. Limited defences exist (e.g., approved trading plans).
hints: Informing a broker does not legitimise the trade.
Sharing UPSI with clients is prohibited.

questions.q: After SEBI's April 2025 relaxation, a research analyst may collect fees in advance from an individual client for a period of up to:
options: One year, if the client agrees
questions.explanation: SEBI's circular of 2 April 2025 allows RAs to collect advance fees for up to one year if the client agrees (earlier limited to one quarter).
hints: That was the earlier rule, since relaxed.

questions.q: A breakout above a resistance level is considered more reliable when it is accompanied by:
questions.explanation: Volume should expand in the direction of the breakout; heavy volume shows conviction behind the move.
hints: An oversold RSI does not fit an upside breakout.

questions.q: Which of the following is a continuation pattern?
questions.explanation: Pennants (like flags) are brief consolidations after a sharp move and usually continue the prior trend. The others are reversal patterns.

questions.q: A doji candlestick, where the open and close are almost equal, primarily signals:
questions.explanation: A doji shows a balance between buyers and sellers. Its meaning depends on context and it needs confirmation from subsequent candles.
hints: A doji has virtually no body - not a trend signal.
It alone does not confirm a reversal.
Gaps are about the open relative to the prior close.
